$comment: Provenance of every art asset in the game. Every file under public/art/ must match an entry (tests/content/art-assets.test.ts). No asset was traced, generated by an image model, or taken from another game. All of it is original work produced by code in this repository, with one approved exception: the conversation portraits (and the man lying in the shade in the teaser film) are built on MakeHuman's CC0 human model (geometry and morph targets only; approved by the owner, Zac Harlan, on 2026-09-26: docs/adr/0016-makehuman-base-for-portraits.md). Those source files are listed under `thirdPartySources`.
projectLicense: No LICENSE file has been chosen for this repository yet, so all rights are reserved by the owner. The assets below are original work made for this project and are covered by whatever licence the owner chooses.

assets.what: Character sprite sheets (idle, breathing, blink, talking, walking, turning; four directions), sheets of people at rest (sitting, lying), sheets with a torn hem, and overlay sheets of story marks (bandages, the spare cloak, a water skin, a lamp, a rolled cloak, a letter case, a lamb carried across the shoulders), with their cast-shadow sheets, for morning, later-day and indoor light, overcast light (under rain cloud), lamp-light (at lamp-lighting, and a house lit by its lamps at night) and moonlight (Chapter 3 adds a newborn lamb held in the arms or the lap, a lamp held up with its flame lit after dark, and a wax tablet; Chapter 2's fishing folk carry an oar or a folded net).
assets.origin: Rendered offline with Blender 5.2 (Cycles) by tools/art/build_people.py. Each person is built by tools/art/lib/world_person.py from the game's character appearance data: a MakeHuman CC0 body (hm08 base mesh and morph targets) shaped by the person's portrait identity (tools/art/lib/world_body.py, portrait_face.identity), rigged with MakeHuman's CC0 default skeleton and skin weights (see thirdPartySources and ADR-0017), with the portrait's skin maps and measured skin correction, hair and beard shells; clothes cut to the body and draped by Blender's cloth simulation (tools/art/lib/world_cloth.py); motion authored here (tools/art/lib/world_motion.py); carried things and story marks from tools/art/lib/people.py. Overlays are rendered with the body as a holdout. No image textures, MakeHuman skins or proxies, downloaded hair or clothing, or image-generation models.
assets.license: Project licence (original work on CC0 MakeHuman data; no attribution required)
assets.rebuild: npm run art:fetch-makehuman && npm run art:people

assets.origin: Rendered offline with Blender 5.2 (Cycles) by tools/art/build_portraits.py from the characters' appearance data (scripts/export-portrait-data.ts) and the casting table (tools/art/lib/portrait_params.py). Heads are MakeHuman's CC0 hm08 base mesh moved by its morph targets (identity: tools/art/lib/portrait_face.py; see thirdPartySources and ADR-0016). Skin shaders and maps, eyes, teeth, hair (Blender hair curves), cloth, lighting and every expression are procedural and original (tools/art/lib/portrait*.py). No image textures, MakeHuman skins or proxies, scanned or other downloaded models, HDRIs, photographs or image-generation models.

assets.what: The teaser film that plays before Chapter 1: teaser.mp4 (H.264), teaser.webm (VP9), both without sound, and poster.webp (a still for before it plays, under reduced motion and offline). 57 s at 24 fps: Jerusalem at sunrise, Aunt Miriam's table, the market, the road down into the wilderness, the ridge path above the gorge, the broken jar below the bend, a man lying in the shade of a rock, the gorge under the title.
assets.origin: Rendered offline with Blender 5.2 (EEVEE) by tools/art/build_teaser.py and cut and encoded with Blender's own FFmpeg by tools/art/edit_teaser.py. Everything in it is procedural and made by code in this repository: the land (tools/art/lib/teaser_land.py: a height field shaped by stream-power erosion), the city, market, room and the scene below the bend (teaser_city.py, teaser_market.py, teaser_room.py, teaser_incident.py), doves and fired clay (teaser_birds.py, teaser_clay.py), and the game's own people (people.py), stones and materials (rocks.py, materials.py). One exception: the man lying in the shade (shot 7, teaser_body.py) is MakeHuman's CC0 hm08 body (geometry and macro key shapes only; see thirdPartySources and the addendum to ADR-0016), posed and dressed (his tunic simulated cloth) here. No other downloaded images, textures, footage, models or music; no image- or video-generation models. The words are not in the film: the game shows them as text, and its music is synthesised in the browser.
assets.rebuild: node scripts/art-build.mjs teaser (then teaser-edit); about 5 hours on an M3 Pro

thirdPartySources.name: MakeHuman hm08 base mesh, morph targets, default skeleton and skin weights
thirdPartySources.use: The body of the man lying in the shade in the Chapter 1 teaser film (shot 7). Head, face and neck geometry of the conversation portraits (the base mesh, its helper geometry for the eyes, lashes, teeth and tongue, and morph targets: macro key shapes for sex, age, muscle, weight and ancestry; face and neck modifiers; asymmetries; expression units), and the bodies of the people in the world (the same base mesh and targets, posed with MakeHuman's default skeleton and its skin weights: rigs/default.mhskel, rigs/default_weights.mhw). No MakeHuman textures, skins, proxies (eyes, brows, lashes, hair, clothes), poses or code.
thirdPartySources.licenseEvidence: makehuman/license.txt section C (assets: base mesh and proxies, targets and modifiers, textures, clothes, poses and expressions released under CC0 1.0 Universal); LICENSE.ASSETS.md (CC0 1.0 legal code); base.obj header ('explicitly released as CC0 in september 2020'). MakeHuman's source code is AGPL-3.0 and is not used.
thirdPartySources.files: 499 files, each with its SHA-256: tools/art/data/makehuman-files.json
